notes.title: The Steam Page for Shipwrecked 64's official followup is now live!
notes.content: [p]Hey everyone! The crew and I have been working real hard for the past year or so, on what is basically an official followup to Shipwrecked 64. While we originally planned something smaller, we have decided that with the current scope of the game, it is best to create a Steam page for it and release it on here, so we did! [/p][p][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3383670/Hotel_Investigation_09/"]You can visit the page here![/url][/p][p]We hope to see y'all ready to play when the time comes, because I can say on behalf of myself and the crew that we're all very, very excited! [/p][p]Thank you all for the continued support, it means the world, genuinely. [/p][p]Toodles![/p]

notes.title: FIRST PATCH OF 2025!!
notes.content:
We finally have a patch!! This is just a bugfix patch to fix some issues I've had for a while. Not a content update, so just be mindful of that. So what changed?
-Starlings no longer stop spawning in Layer 3
-Bugfixes in the Volcano level (which will soon be revamped). Bucky no longer can get caught in spawn loop
-Duncan Dolphin has been rehomed.
-Minor environmental changes to Layer 0-4 (You may not notice that many of them)
-Fixed about as much Layer 4 pathing as I could for Blot (Keep me in the loop on that though since he's always given me issues)
-Minor construction

More content to be added soon! I've been wrapped up in development of our followup, HI-09, but more will be done soon enough!

Toodles! Thank you so much for the last year of support. You guys are all the best! :)

Removed the SOBT puzzle noone liked

notes.title: Hotfix 3
notes.content:
-AI can now despawn on the boss, meaning they can no longer camp areas
-EnemyManager has longer timer in the boss

notes.title: Hotfix 2
notes.content:
-Fixed a minor bug in Layer 2 where players could get stuck behind invisible collision 
-HEAVILY nerfed Layer 3 Plaza opening, allowing players to safely figure out most puzzles without being immediately swamped by enemies
-Buffed Layer 3 AI during the actual tasks you have to perform that don't involve puzzles (Batteries and turning on PCs)
-Removed Duncan Dolphin

The next update will be heavier in terms of actually changing the player experience and mass-fixing bugs, but I wanted to take baby steps since I only got back home a few days back. 

Toodle-oo!!

notes.title: First Steam Post!
notes.content:
[b]Hello Children of the Cogs![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43382792/3ced13127d56084a88291cf2bdbb767f8c79d5b3.gif[/img]

This is the lead dev of the Shipwrecked 64 recovery project, Squeaks D'Corgeh! It's very nice to have seen so much enthusiasm towards the game so far! 

I know that we've been pretty silent on the Steam side of things, but it's not for no reason! The team's had our noses down and working very hard trying to get the game from a mess of jumbled code to a fully playable experience once again, and even enhancing some things, like, if it weren't for us modifying the game, you would still be stuck using an automatic camera and pressing a button to snap it back into place, very unfortunate, ain't it. Don't worry, for those of you who want the full original experience, we will be leaving that in the game as an option, as well as instructions on how to hook up that old dusty controller of yours! 

Now, the game itself has actually been growing a lot in size as we discover more files. There's already multiple endings, a lot of secrets you'll have to really look to find, and even some investigative work. Rest assured, when you play this game, you can play it normally if you wish, but you can also put on your detective hat, and help us decipher this game and it's meaning! 

I've actually gotten some people from my circles to test this game a few times, as I'm curious to their player experiences. I've seen headphones thrown, people genuinely reporting feeling scared to a point of feeling queasy, and I've heard many screams, whether they're screaming profanities, or yelling about how cool something is, everyone seems to be engaging with the game so far and it really has put a smile on my face to finally introduce Cogware's flagship game to the world. 

My personal favorite part of the game has been the puzzle-like nature of the game, and I'm not just talking about the levels. Testers are finding new things all the time, and it's very fun to see them using the tools laid out in front of them to explore. I'm hoping to share that same feeling to all of you in due time!

That's all for now, folks, thanks for reading my update! Toodle-oo!
